title: Legacy CRM iPhone User Guide — Mobile UX Foundation and Common Functions
summary: The mobile user experience foundation for a legacy life sciences CRM iPhone application, covering the home page dashboard architecture, common interaction patterns, display density modes, advanced search, quick actions, web viewer, attachments, dark mode support, and the embedded AI assistant for field representatives.

findings.home_page_architecture: The home page serves as the central dashboard for field representatives, composed of configurable widget sections: Messages (system and manager communications), Up Next (algorithmically prioritized upcoming activities), Next Best Customer recommendations (scoring-based account prioritization), Activity Plan Chart (visual progress against cyclical visit targets), Sales Chart (territory performance visualization with trend indicators), and Dashboard Reports (configurable report widgets rendered as tabular summaries or charts). Each widget section can be independently enabled or disabled through admin configuration, and the layout adapts to the representative's profile and role.
findings.common_functions_and_navigation: Common interaction patterns span the entire application: Display Density toggles between Comfy (spacious layout with larger touch targets) and Compact (dense layout showing more data per screen) modes. Page Notifications surface contextual alerts within individual record views. Recent Activity provides quick access to recently viewed or modified records. Data Entry Fields support type-specific input controls (text, picklist, date picker, lookup, multi-select). Advanced Search enables cross-object search with field-specific filters and saved search configurations. Quick Actions provide configurable shortcut buttons for frequently used operations. The Web Viewer renders external web content within the application shell. Attachments support file upload, camera capture, and document viewing inline.
findings.dark_mode_and_display: The application supports system-level dark mode, inverting the color scheme for reduced eye strain during low-light field visits (early morning or evening appointments). Dark mode applies across all screens including the home page, record views, CLM presentations (where content-specific rendering is handled separately), and the planner calendar. The display adapts to the system accessibility settings for font size scaling.
findings.ai_assistant_integration: An embedded AI assistant provides conversational support for field representatives directly within the application. The assistant can help with record lookup, scheduling guidance, account information retrieval, and answering questions about platform features. The assistant operates within the security context of the authenticated user, accessing only data the representative is authorized to view.

title: Legacy CRM iPhone User Guide — Account Management, Profiles, and Address Administration
summary: The account management and profile architecture for a legacy life sciences CRM iPhone application, covering account search and creation workflows, profile page composition with location maps and customer intelligence sections, address management with best-time scheduling, data change validation, opt-in/opt-out management, and document management capabilities.

findings.account_search_and_creation: Account management supports multiple discovery patterns: text search across account names and identifiers, filtered list views with configurable sort criteria, bulk update operations for field-level changes across multiple accounts, and Search Before Create duplicate detection during new account creation. Account creation enforces required field validation and territory assignment rules. Account lists support configurable column display, inline editing for quick updates, and filter persistence across sessions.
findings.account_profile_composition: The account profile page is a composite view assembled from multiple data sources: Location Map (geographic visualization of the account address with directions integration), Highlights (key account metrics and status indicators), Customer Information (demographic and classification fields), Territory Fields (territory assignment and alignment data), Sales Chart (account-specific sales trend visualization), Details (full field-level record display organized by sections), Product Restrictions (account-level product access limitations), Related Records (child objects including calls, meetings, orders, and activities), Attachments (documents and files associated with the account), Opt Information (communication preference and consent status), Affiliations (organizational relationships and parent-child hierarchies), and Ratings (profiling scores and segmentation data from rating assessments).
findings.address_management: Address management supports full lifecycle operations: adding new addresses to accounts, creating addresses during account creation, modifying existing address records, and configuring Best Times metadata (optimal visit windows by day of week and time slot). Best Times data informs the planner and routing engine to suggest visit schedules that align with provider availability patterns. Addresses carry geographic coordinates for map rendering and distance calculations.
findings.data_change_and_opt_management: Data Change Validation enforces business rules on field modifications — specific fields can be locked, require approval workflows, or trigger notifications when changed. Opt Management provides the interface for recording healthcare provider communication preferences: opt-in and opt-out status per channel (email, phone, in-person, digital), consent capture with timestamp and source tracking, and compliance enforcement that prevents communication through opted-out channels. Document Management enables file attachment, viewing, and organization at the account level.

title: Legacy CRM iPhone User Guide — Planner, Calendar, and Scheduling
summary: The planner and calendar architecture for a legacy life sciences CRM iPhone application, covering the multi-view calendar with event type filtering, shared calendar visibility, scheduling workflows for calls/meetings/coaching events, route planning, time-off territory management, bulk operations, reminders, and team schedule viewing for managers.

findings.planner_views_and_navigation: The planner provides day, week, and month calendar views with swipe-based navigation between time periods. Each view renders events as color-coded blocks differentiated by event type (calls, meetings, coaching events, general events, time off). Event Type Filters allow representatives to toggle visibility of specific event categories, reducing visual clutter when focusing on particular activity types. The planner integrates with the device calendar for cross-referencing personal and professional schedules.
findings.event_creation_and_management: The planner supports creation and management of multiple event types: To-Dos (task-based items with due dates and completion tracking), General Events (non-CRM events for schedule blocking), Time Off Territory (representative absence periods that affect territory coverage calculations), Calls (field visits scheduled against accounts — the primary field activity), Booking Agent Calls (scheduled through an agent-based booking system), Meetings (formal events with full attendee and logistics management), and Field Coaching Events (supervisor-subordinate evaluation sessions). Bulk deletion enables removing multiple events simultaneously when schedule changes require wholesale rescheduling.
findings.routes_and_shared_calendar: Route planning organizes daily or weekly call sequences geographically, optimizing travel between account locations. Routes display on a map view with driving directions between stops and estimated travel times. The Shared Calendar feature provides visibility into other representatives' schedules within the same territory or team, enabling coordination for joint calls, coverage during absences, and manager oversight. Reminders can be configured per event with customizable advance notification periods.
findings.team_schedule_and_coaching: My Team Schedule Viewer provides managers and district managers with a consolidated view of their team's planned activities, enabling identification of coverage gaps, workload imbalances, and coaching opportunities. The team view aggregates across all direct reports with drill-down to individual representative schedules. Field Coaching Events appear in both the coach's and employee's calendars with status tracking through the evaluation lifecycle.

title: Legacy CRM iPhone User Guide — CLM Presentations and Content Delivery
summary: The closed-loop marketing presentation experience for a legacy life sciences CRM iPhone application, covering product-restricted content filtering, targeted and recommended presentation algorithms, the interactive presentation player, email-based CLM content sharing, field email template management, messaging platform content sharing, and survey execution for accounts.

findings.content_filtering_and_recommendations: CLM content access is filtered by Product Restrictions — account-level and territory-level product configurations determine which presentations and sequences are available for display during field interactions. Three content discovery modes exist: Targeted presentations (algorithmically matched to the current account based on specialty, therapeutic area, and engagement history), Recommended presentations (prioritized by marketing based on campaign objectives and product messaging strategies), and Favorite presentations (representative-curated personal collections for quick access to frequently used content).
findings.presentation_player: The presentation player renders HTML5 content within an embedded WebKit view with full gesture support: swipe navigation between slides, pinch-to-zoom for detailed content inspection, and tap interactions for hyperlinks and embedded media. The player tracks slide-level engagement data (dwell time, navigation patterns, interaction events) automatically for closed-loop analytics. Content can branch between slides based on conversation direction, and the player supports landscape orientation for optimal content display.
findings.email_and_messaging_distribution: Email CLM Content enables representatives to send approved presentations to healthcare providers via compliant email, with the content embedded or attached according to template configuration. Field Email Templates provide pre-approved email content with dynamic merge fields (provider name, product details, representative information) and compliance-approved messaging. Templates support territory-based availability and version management. Messaging platform content sharing extends CLM distribution to supported messaging channels with content adaptation for the target platform's rendering constraints.
findings.surveys_for_accounts: Surveys can be executed in the context of account interactions, collecting structured responses through configurable question types (multiple choice, rating scales, free text, slider inputs). Survey responses are linked to the originating account and interaction record, enabling longitudinal analysis of provider sentiment and feedback across visits. Survey completion status tracks which providers have been surveyed and which are pending.

title: Legacy CRM iPhone User Guide — Field Execution: Calls, Sampling, and Compliance
summary: The field execution workflow for a legacy life sciences CRM iPhone application, covering the complete call lifecycle from creation through submission, including call validation rules, product message delivery, sample and DTP disbursement with compliance controls, electronic signature capture, attendee management, expense tracking, follow-up actions, and call history.

findings.call_lifecycle_and_validation: Calls are the primary field execution record, representing in-person visits to healthcare providers. Call Rules and Validation enforce business constraints: required fields based on call type, territory-based call frequency limits, time-based restrictions (minimum duration, maximum per day), and product-specific compliance requirements. The call creation flow captures General Information (account, date/time, location), Pre-Call Objectives (planned discussion topics), and configures the call type which determines available sections and required data.
findings.call_sections_and_content: A call record is composed of multiple configurable sections: Post-Call Objectives (outcomes and next steps), Compliance (regulatory tracking fields), Attendees (additional participants beyond the primary provider), Child Calls (sub-interactions within a group visit), CLM (presentations shown during the visit with engagement tracking), Messages (key messages delivered with product associations), Details (custom fields and notes), Samples (product samples disbursed with lot tracking), DTP (Direct-to-Physician shipments), Items (non-sample product items left with the provider), Employees (internal participants), Expenses (visit-related costs), Attachments (photos, documents captured during the visit), Follow-up (scheduled next actions), and configurable Buttons (custom actions available during the call).
findings.sampling_and_dtp_compliance: Sample disbursement requires: product and lot selection from the representative's current inventory, quantity entry with validation against available stock and regulatory limits, healthcare provider state license validation (system blocks disbursement for inactive or revoked licenses), and receipt verification through electronic signature capture or document ID recording. DTP (Direct-to-Physician) disbursements follow a parallel workflow where samples are shipped directly to the provider's office rather than hand-delivered, requiring additional chain-of-custody documentation and shipping address confirmation. Both methods enforce 21 CFR Part 203 compliance requirements.
findings.signature_submission_and_history: Electronic signature capture uses the device touchscreen for provider signature recording, which is stored as part of the call record for regulatory compliance. The signature satisfies 21 CFR Part 11 requirements for electronic records and signatures. After completing all required sections, the Submit action finalizes the call record, making it read-only and triggering server-side processing (inventory updates, compliance calculations, analytics aggregation). Delay Reason captures why a call was not submitted immediately. Actions for Accounts provides quick-access operations available directly from account context during calls. Call History displays a chronological log of all previous visits to the current account.

title: Legacy CRM iPhone User Guide — Meetings and Events Management
summary: The comprehensive meetings and events management workflow for a legacy life sciences CRM iPhone application, covering the full event lifecycle from creation through closure, including attendee management with nomination and consent workflows, budget and expense tracking with allocation, expense system integration, signature capture with QR and print sign-in, survey execution, and multi-status approval workflows.

findings.meeting_lifecycle_and_creation: Meetings represent formal events such as speaker programs, educational seminars, advisory boards, and promotional gatherings. Meeting Rules and Validation enforce business constraints on event creation and modification. The creation flow supports search for existing meetings, new meeting creation with comprehensive detail capture, and cloning of past meetings as templates. Meeting records contain Highlights (key metrics summary), Details with Attendee Counts and Expense Summary, Locations (venue information), and Topics (agenda items and discussion points).
findings.attendee_management: Attendee management is the most complex subsystem within meetings: Quotas enforce limits on attendee counts by type (healthcare providers, internal employees, speakers). HCP Nomination enables field representatives to propose providers for invitation, subject to approval workflows. Speaker management tracks contracted speakers with Fair Market Value compliance. Consent capture records attendee agreement to participation terms. Status tracking follows each attendee through the invitation lifecycle (invited, confirmed, attended, no-show, cancelled). Address management links attendees to specific practice locations for logistics planning. Email and Print Invitations provide both digital and physical invitation distribution channels.
findings.budget_expense_and_integration: Budget management defines financial allocations for meetings with tracking against actual expenditures. Estimated Expenses capture planned costs during meeting planning. Actual Expenses record real costs after execution, with allocation rules distributing expenses across cost centers or funding sources. Receipts can be photographed and attached to expense line items. The system integrates with external expense management platforms for automated expense report creation and approval routing, linking meeting expenses to the originating event for compliance audit trails.
findings.signatures_surveys_and_workflow: Attendee sign-in supports multiple capture methods: QR Code scan (attendees scan a meeting-specific QR code from their device), Print Sign-In Sheet (physical sign-in sheets for venues without reliable connectivity), and individual electronic signature capture. Surveys can be administered to attendees during or after the event. The meeting status workflow follows a defined progression: Submit (representative submits for approval), Approve/Reject (manager reviews), Execute (event takes place), Conclude (post-event wrap-up with final expense entry), Close (administrative finalization), with Reopen and Cancel available at appropriate stages. Meeting History provides a complete audit trail of all status transitions with timestamps and actors.

title: Legacy CRM iPhone User Guide — Planning, Compliance, Medical Inquiries, and Coaching
summary: The planning, compliance, and professional development capabilities of a legacy life sciences CRM iPhone application, covering activity plans for cyclical visit targeting, account plan management with business objectives and stakeholder mapping, regulatory compliance tracking for educational events, medical inquiry submission, insight capture and collaboration, study management, coaching event workflows, reporting, and application settings.

findings.activity_and_account_planning: Activity Plans define cyclical visit targets — the frequency and product focus for each account over a planning period, with progress tracking against targets displayed as completion percentages. Account Plan Management provides strategic planning capabilities: Business Objectives define territory-level goals, Territory Plans link objectives to geographic assignments, Sprints break objectives into time-boxed execution periods, Account Plans map strategies to individual accounts, Tactics specify the actions to achieve objectives, To-Dos track granular tasks within tactics, and Stakeholders identify key decision-makers and influencers within target accounts.
findings.compliance_tracking: Account Compliances encompass two regulatory tracking frameworks: EPPV (Educational Event Post-Visit Payment) tracks compliance with payment limits and reporting requirements for healthcare provider attendance at educational events, and MID (Medical Information Disclosure) tracks compliance with medical information sharing regulations. Both frameworks support View (current compliance status), Complete (mark requirement as fulfilled), and Skip (bypass with documented reason) operations. Compliance status integrates with the call and meeting workflows to prevent interactions that would violate regulatory limits.
findings.medical_inquiries_and_insights: Medical Inquiries 2.0 provides a structured workflow for capturing and routing clinical questions from healthcare providers to medical affairs teams. The inquiry record captures the question, relevant therapeutic area, urgency level, and provider context, then routes through a defined approval and response workflow. Insights enable field representatives to capture observations, competitive intelligence, and market signals from field interactions. The Insights Board provides a collaborative view where team members can browse, upvote (indicating agreement or importance), filter by category, and create new insights. Individual insight records contain details, supporting evidence, and associated accounts.
findings.coaching_studies_and_reporting: Studies management tracks clinical trial sites and staff assignments relevant to the representative's territory. Coaching Events follow a structured evaluation workflow: Search (find existing events), Create (initiate a new coaching session), Self-Evaluation (employee completes pre-assessment), Evaluate Employee (coach conducts assessment using configurable coaching form templates with scored questions), Development Plan (document growth areas and action items), Publish (share results with the employee), Review (employee acknowledges), Finish (close the coaching cycle), and Cancel (terminate if needed). Reports provide configurable data views with filtering and export capabilities. App Settings allow representatives to customize application behavior including sync preferences, notification settings, and display options.
